title: Microsoft Entra ID Governance: account discovery finds local and unassigned accounts in provisioned apps
summary: The briefing's roadmap details, licensing, discovery behaviour and automation are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The attribute-mapping route needs only the Edit Attribute screen name added; no blocking findings were found.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and GCC.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Discovery is on as an available capability for licensed administrators on supported connectors.
claims.quote: Account discovery is enabled for all provisioning connectors except those listed below.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; summary; Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; Scope
claims.claim: Account Discovery requires the Microsoft Entra ID Governance add-on or Microsoft Entra Suite, supporting the add-on licensing model.
claims.quote: Account Discovery requires the Microsoft Entra ID Governance add-on or Microsoft Entra Suite.

claims.claim: The licensing fundamentals page publishes no price specific to Account Discovery.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra account discovery pricing meter charge discovery runs Governance license. Read licensing-fundamentals, including Account Discovery, Features by license and Licensing FAQs, and how-to-account-discovery; no discovery-specific price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the feature page nor the licensing fundamentals page documents a separate discovery-run meter or charge in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra account discovery pricing meter charge discovery runs Governance license. Opened how-to-account-discovery and licensing-fundamentals in full; neither documents a separate discovery-run meter or charge.

claims.claim: Administrators can discover unmanaged accounts in applications configured for Microsoft Entra provisioning.
claims.quote: The discovery report helps you identify local or orphan identities both during initial onboarding and during ongoing provisioning operations.

claims.claim: Discover identities retrieves users and groups from the target application.
claims.quote: Account discovery uses the Discover identities experience to retrieve users and groups from a target application

claims.claim: Discovery matches target users and groups to corresponding Microsoft Entra ID users and groups.
claims.quote: match them to corresponding users and groups in Microsoft Entra ID, and classify the results so you can bring unmanaged identities under governance.

claims.claim: The discovery experience classifies identities into Local, Unassigned and Assigned categories.
claims.quote: Account discovery retrieves users and groups from a target application and classifies them into three categories:

claims.claim: Local identities have no corresponding Microsoft Entra ID user or group.
claims.quote: Local identities — Users or groups in the target application that have no corresponding user or group in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What's changing: Local identities; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Local identities may be former employees whose application accounts were not deprovisioned.
claims.quote: Former employees whose directory accounts were removed but whose application accounts weren't deprovisioned.

claims.where: What's changing: Local identities; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Local identities may be service or shared accounts created directly in the application.
claims.quote: Service accounts or shared accounts created directly in the application.

claims.claim: Local identities may be users provisioned through a separate process.
claims.quote: Users provisioned through a separate process that didn't use Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Local identities may be groups created directly in the target application.
claims.quote: Groups created directly in the target application.

claims.where: What's changing: Local identities; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Mismatched or outdated attribute values can prevent a match and produce local identities.
claims.quote: identities that didn't match due to data quality issues (for example, mismatched or outdated attribute values).

claims.claim: Unassigned identities match an Entra identity but lack enterprise-application assignment, so provisioning does not manage them.
claims.quote: Unassigned identities — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID but aren't assigned to the enterprise application. These identities exist in your directory but don't have the required application assignment for provisioning to manage them.

claims.claim: Assigned identities match an Entra identity, are assigned to the application and are managed by provisioning.
claims.quote: Assigned identities — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID and are assigned to the enterprise application. These identities are fully managed by the provisioning service.

claims.claim: Discovery uses an application's provisioning configuration with valid credentials and a successful test connection.
claims.quote: An enterprise application configured for provisioning with valid credentials and a successful test connection.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Discovery requires a direct matching attribute mapping.
claims.quote: A direct matching attribute mapping configured between Microsoft Entra ID and the target application.

claims.claim: If multiple matching attributes are configured, discovery uses only the first.
claims.quote: If multiple matching attributes are configured, only the first matching attribute is used.

claims.claim: Expression-based transformations are not supported for discovery matching.
claims.quote: Account discovery requires a direct matching attribute for correlation. Expression-based transformations aren't supported for matching.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents account discovery as enabled for all provisioning connectors except its listed exclusions.
claims.quote: Account discovery is enabled for all provisioning connectors except those listed below.

claims.claim: Group discovery, including group memberships, is in preview.
claims.quote: Group discovery, including group memberships, is currently in preview.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A discovery report takes at least 30 minutes to generate.
claims.quote: The discovery takes at least 30 minutes to generate a report.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example says an application with 250,000 identities might take 12 hours or more.
claims.quote: For example, an application with 250,000 identities might take 12 hours or more to generate a discovery report.

claims.claim: Discovered accounts can be reviewed in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: In addition to reviewing discovered accounts in the Microsoft Entra admin center, you can use Microsoft Graph to programmatically retrieve Account discovery results.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta identity correlation APIs retrieve discovery results.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft Graph beta API to: List identity correlation reports in the tenant. Retrieve a specific identity correlation report. List the identities included in a report. Filter identities by correlation status.

claims.claim: Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise provides preview investigation of account discovery reports.
claims.quote: Investigate account discovery with the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise (preview). You can use the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise to investigate account discovery reports by asking questions in natural language.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 to assign discovered correlated users to the enterprise application.
claims.quote: Assign all correlated users to the enterprise application: pwsh -File '.\Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1' -ServicePrincipalId "7A22..."

claims.claim: The script can assign users to access packages using a rules file.
claims.quote: Assign all correlated users to a specific access package by using an example rules file: pwsh -File '.\Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1' -ServicePrincipalId '7A22...' -RulesFile '.\access-package-rules-internal.csv' -DryRun -OutputFile '.\results-dryrun.csv'

claims.claim: Application administrators can manually create application accounts after provisioning onboarding.
claims.quote: After onboarding to provisioning, application administrators can manually create accounts in the application.

claims.claim: Discovery identifies unmanaged identities that can subsequently be brought into access packages, reviews and lifecycle workflows.
claims.quote: After you discover identities in your target applications, you can: Assign existing users to your access packages to govern access going forward, run reviews on the access packages to certify access, and configure lifecycle workflows to automate lifecycle management.

claims.claim: An administrator starts a discovery report by selecting Discover identities.
claims.quote: Select Discover identities. The provisioning service retrieves users and groups from the target application and displays them organized by category.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationales: risk and impact
claims.claim: Discovery reports identities rather than assigning or removing them; those changes require separate administrator actions.
claims.quote: Review these identities to determine whether they should be removed from the target application, matched to an existing user or group in Microsoft Entra ID, or kept as-is. To bring these identities under provisioning management: ... Assign the appropriate users or groups to the application.

claims.claim: The report imports account attributes from the target application.
claims.quote: Manage columns to view the imported attributes from the target application and the correlation status.

claims.claim: View attributes displays an individual discovered user's attributes.
claims.quote: You can find property names in the discovery experience by selecting View attributes for an individual user or by reviewing your provisioning attribute mappings.

claims.claim: Global Reader, Reports Reader and Security Reader can read Graph correlation reports even though they are not among discovery-run prerequisite roles.
claims.quote: This operation supports the following built-in roles ... Global Reader ... Reports Reader ... Security Reader

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Discovery prerequisites name Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator or Hybrid Identity Administrator.
claims.quote: One of the following roles: Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, or Hybrid Identity Administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls; controls[3]
claims.claim: Assigning matched but unassigned identities to the application brings them under provisioning management on subsequent cycles.
claims.quote: Assign the appropriate users or groups to the application. After assignment, the provisioning service manages these identities on subsequent provisioning cycles.

claims.claim: Provisioning management can update users' target-application attributes.
claims.quote: If you enable user provisioning for a non-Microsoft SaaS application, the Microsoft Entra admin center controls its attribute values through attribute-mappings.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The script's -DryRun previews actions without changing anything.
claims.quote: -DryRun | Shows what would happen without making any changes.

claims.claim: The script's -OutputFile records a CSV audit trail.
claims.quote: -OutputFile | Creates a full audit trail as a CSV file with timestamps, actions, and error details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Target applications must implement SCIM pagination under RFC 7644 Section 3.4.2.4.
claims.quote: For account discovery to work, the target application must implement SCIM pagination as described in RFC 7644, Section 3.4.2.4. ... If your discovery report has zero results ... verify with the application vendor that the application supports pagination

claims.where: Scope: Not supported; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Discovery excludes Adobe Identity Management, AWS, Cloud sync, cross-tenant/cloud synchronisation, Freshservice, AD group provisioning and HR provisioning including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, HiBob and API-driven provisioning.
claims.quote: Adobe Identity Management, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Cloud sync, Cross-tenant synchronization and cross-cloud synchronization, Freshservice, Group provisioning to Active Directory, HR provisioning (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, HiBob, and API-driven provisioning)

claims.claim: ECMA, Google Cloud and Google Workspace support user discovery but not group discovery.
claims.quote: The following connectors and provisioning scenarios support user discovery, but don't support group discovery at this time: ECMA, Google Cloud, and Google Workspace.

claims.claim: Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise and identity correlation APIs are not currently available in sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: Use the global Microsoft cloud. Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise and the identity correlation APIs aren't currently available in sovereign clouds.

claims.claim: The Graph list correlation API is available in the global service, not US Government L4, US Government L5 (DOD) or China.
claims.quote: | Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | ... | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: Discovery is reached through Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications > application > Provisioning > Discover identities.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications. Select the application you want to discover identities for. In the left navigation, select Provisioning. ... Select Discover identities.

claims.claim: No automation operation to start or schedule an account discovery run is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: account discovery start discovery run schedule Microsoft Graph identityCorrelation enable default provisioning connectors. Opened how-to-account-discovery and identitycorrelation beta reference; only UI initiation and read operations are documented.

claims.claim: The report can be reached through Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications > application > Provisioning > Discover identities.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications. ... select Provisioning. ... Select Discover identities. The provisioning service retrieves users and groups from the target application and displays them organized by category.

claims.claim: GET /beta/reports/correlations lists tenant identity correlation reports.
claims.quote: List the identityCorrelation reports in the tenant. ... GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/reports/correlations

claims.claim: The matching setting is reached through Entra ID > Enterprise apps > app > Provisioning > Manage > Attribute Mapping > mapping > Match objects using this attribute.
claims.quote: Under Manage, select Attribute Mapping. ... To edit an existing mapping, select the pencil icon to the right of the mapping row. The Edit Attribute screen opens ... Match objects using this attribute
claims.fix: Set controls[2].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Entra ID > Enterprise apps > app > Provisioning > Manage > Attribute Mapping > mapping > Edit Attribute > Match objects using this attribute', adding the screen heading documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/app-provisioning/customize-application-attributes.

claims.claim: PUT /v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/synchronization/jobs/{jobId}/schema updates the provisioning job's schema.
claims.quote: This method fully replaces the current schema with the one provided in the request. ... PUT https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/synchronization/jobs/{jobId}/schema

claims.claim: The schema's attribute mappings carry matchingPriority, which determines initial provisioning matching.
claims.quote: matchingPriority | Int32 | If higher than 0, this attribute will be used to perform an initial match of the objects between source and target directories. The synchronization engine will try to find the matching object using attribute with lowest value of matching priority first.

claims.claim: The application assignment page is reached through Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications > application > Users and groups.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications. Select the application ... To bring these identities under provisioning management: Navigate to the enterprise application's Users and groups page. Assign the appropriate users or groups to the application.

claims.claim: pwsh -File '.\Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1' -ServicePrincipalId <service principal id> assigns correlated users to the enterprise application.
claims.quote: Download the Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 file and run it in PowerShell 7.x to assign users. ... Assign all correlated users to the enterprise application: pwsh -File '.\Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1' -ServicePrincipalId "7A22..."

claims.where: Governance controls; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The identityCorrelation reference lists only List, Get and List identities read operations.
claims.quote: Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported. ... List ... Get a list ... Get ... Read the properties and relationships ... List identities ... List the correlated identities for this identity correlation report.

claims.claim: ProvisioningLog.Read.All is the least-privileged permission for delegated work or school access to list correlation reports.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All ... Application | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All ... the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation.

claims.claim: P1 or P2 alone does not entitle tenants to Account Discovery.
claims.quote: | Feature | Free | Microsoft Entra ID P1 | Microsoft Entra ID P2 | Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Entra Suite | Microsoft Agent 365 | Microsoft 365 E7 | ... | Account Discovery |  |  |  | ✅ | ✅ |  | ✅ |

claims.claim: ProvisioningLog.Read.All is the least-privileged permission for application access to list correlation reports.
claims.quote: | Application | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All |

claims.claim: Delegated users additionally need a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role granting the operation's permissions.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support the beta correlation APIs for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to run Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 in PowerShell 7.x.
claims.quote: Download the Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 file and run it in PowerShell 7.x to assign users.

claims.claim: Missing SCIM pagination support can explain zero discovery results.
claims.quote: If your discovery report has zero results, verify that you configured a single direct matching attribute (no expressions) in your attribute mappings. Next, verify with the application vendor that the application supports pagination

claims.claim: The Graph synchronizationSchema update replaces the whole current schema with the request body.
claims.quote: This method fully replaces the current schema with the one provided in the request.

claims.claim: Manage columns lets administrators view imported target-application attributes and correlation status.
claims.quote: Manage columns to view the imported attributes from the target application and the correlation status.

claims.where: Scope: Not supported; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: LinkedIn Learning, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, N-able, ServiceNow and Snowflake do not support discovery.
claims.quote: The following connectors and provisioning scenarios don't support user or group discovery at this time: ... LinkedIn Learning, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, N-able, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.

claims.claim: AuditLog.Read.All is also accepted for delegated work or school access to list correlation reports.
claims.quote: | Delegated (work or school account) | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All |

claims.claim: AuditLog.Read.All is also accepted for application access to list correlation reports.
claims.quote: | Application | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All |
